meta.description: Looking for a Wallos alternative? Compare Coinio and Wallos on setup, reminders, currencies, AI and households, and see how to import your Wallos data.
og.title: Coinio vs Wallos: an honest comparison
og.description: Two self-hosted subscription trackers side by side, who each one suits, and how to move from Wallos to Coinio.
crumb.label: Breadcrumb
page.title: A Wallos alternative, compared honestly
page.lede: Coinio is a free, MIT-licensed subscription tracker that runs as one Docker image and imports your Wallos export, with family & shared splits and passkey sign-in. Wallos is the older, bigger project, with independent multi-user accounts, OIDC sign-in and six notification channels. Which one fits depends on your workflow and how you want to be reminded.
page.checked: Facts about Wallos come from its README and website, checked on 20 November 2026.
cta.note: Run this on a server with Docker. No account with us and no API key.
glance.title: Coinio and Wallos at a glance
glance.lede: Both are open source, both keep everything in SQLite on your own server, and both roll every currency into one total. They differ in reminders, sign-in, AI features and how much there is to set up.
row.install.coinio: One-line script or one Docker image (amd64, arm64). No separate database, no API key.
row.install.wallos: Docker image, or bare metal with PHP 8.3, nginx or Apache, and a set of cron jobs.
row.languages.coinio: 8: English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese
row.currency.coinio: Each subscription keeps its own currency. Daily ECB rates through Frankfurter, no key needed. Any ISO currency, including zero-decimal ones such as JPY and KRW.
row.currency.wallos: Multiple currencies. Conversion uses the Fixer API, which needs a free API key.
row.reminders.coinio: Email (SMTP), Telegram (including forum topics), Discord, Slack, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover, webhook and Apprise (100+ services). Several reminders per subscription, an overdue alert, weekly and monthly digests, alerts for ending free trials, exceeded monthly budgets and price changes, and fully editable message templates.
row.reminders.wallos: Email, Discord, Pushover, Telegram, Gotify and webhooks.
row.ai.coinio: Built-in MCP server with OAuth: Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP clients can read and update your subscriptions.
row.ai.wallos: AI saving tips from ChatGPT, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API. No MCP server in its README.
row.iphone.coinio: Scriptable widgets for the Home Screen and Lock Screen, plus an installable web app.
row.iphone.wallos: Responsive mobile layout. No widget in its README.
row.custom.coinio: Four themes plus system, accent colour, six font pairs, card order, custom CSS and sandboxed HTML cards.
row.custom.wallos: Themes, custom categories and display options.
row.users.coinio: Family & shared household: member profiles with roles, single-use invite links, equal/custom splits, private personal subs, and passkey login.
row.users.wallos: Household members and multiple user accounts.
row.oidc.wallos: Yes, OIDC with OAuth, also configurable through environment variables.
row.demo.coinio: The real app running in your browser with sample data. No sign-in.
row.demo.wallos: demo.wallosapp.com, sign in with demo / demo. Resets every two hours.
pick.title: Which one should you pick?
pick.lede: Pick Wallos if you need independent multi-tenant admin accounts or OIDC sign-in. Pick Coinio if you want shared family splits with private personal subs, passkey login, AI assistants, an iPhone widget and zero-fuss setup.
pick.wallos.title: Wallos is the better fit if
pick.wallos.1: you need fully separate multi-tenant logins with independent settings per user;
pick.wallos.2: you sign in through an identity provider with OIDC;
pick.wallos.3: you prefer a mature project: Wallos dates from 2023, has about 8,900 GitHub stars and its own Discord server;
pick.wallos.4: you need an interface language Coinio does not have yet;
pick.wallos.5: you want to run it on plain PHP without Docker.
pick.coinio.title: Coinio is the better fit if
pick.coinio.1: you want to ask Claude or ChatGPT what renews this week, or have them mark a bill paid;
pick.coinio.2: you want upcoming payments on your iPhone Home Screen or Lock Screen;
pick.coinio.3: you would rather not sign up for an exchange-rate API key;
pick.coinio.4: you like to change the look: themes, fonts, your own CSS or HTML cards;
pick.coinio.5: you want the permissive MIT license;
pick.coinio.6: you want shared family plans with personal privacy and passwordless passkey sign-in.
pick.note: To be fair about it: Coinio is a younger project (v0.4) that also offers free cloud hosting at app.getcoinio.me, passkeys, shared family splits and Firefly III sync. Wallos has years of fixes and a much larger community.
move.title: Moving from Wallos to Coinio
move.lede: Coinio reads the JSON file that Wallos exports. You see every subscription and any warnings before anything is saved, and the import is all or nothing.
move.step1: In Wallos, open Settings and use Export subscriptions to download the JSON file.
move.step2: In Coinio, open Settings › Import (or Import from Wallos in the welcome steps) and pick the file. Files up to 1 MB are accepted.
move.step3: Check the list and the warnings, then click Import. Either every row is imported or none is.
move.carry.title: What carries over
move.carry.body: Name, price and currency, billing cycle, next payment, automatic renewal, website (for the logo), category, payment method, Paid By (mapped to household members), notes, and whether the subscription is active. State, Notifications and Cancellation Date are left out. Daily cycles are not supported, and each price needs a currency code or symbol.
move.docs: Full field mapping in the docs
pfaq.title: Coinio and Wallos, briefly
pfaq.better.a: Neither is better for everyone. Wallos has OIDC sign-in and a longer track record. Coinio adds shared family plans with custom splits, passwordless passkey sign-in, no API key for exchange rates, an MCP server for AI assistants, an iPhone widget and deeper visual customization.
pfaq.import.q: Can I import my data from Wallos?
pfaq.import.a: Yes. Export your subscriptions from Wallos as JSON and load the file in Coinio under Settings › Import. Coinio shows a preview with warnings first and saves nothing until you confirm. The import guide lists how each field is mapped.
pfaq.both.q: Can I run Coinio and Wallos side by side?
pfaq.both.a: Yes. They are separate containers with their own data. Wallos's examples publish port 8282 and Coinio uses 8080, so the defaults don't clash, and you can try Coinio before you switch.
pfaq.notify.q: Does Coinio send email or Discord notifications?
pfaq.notify.a: Yes. Coinio sends email (SMTP), Telegram (including forum topics), Discord, Slack, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover and generic webhook notifications, and reaches 100+ more services through Apprise. You can set several reminders per subscription, get an overdue alert and weekly or monthly digests, and edit every message template.
pfaq.free.a: Yes. Coinio is MIT-licensed, with no paid tier and no account with us. Wallos is free as well, under GPL-3.0.
final.title: Try Coinio next to Wallos.
final.lede: Install it in a minute, import your Wallos file and keep whichever suits you.
